items.description: filing a stock level (unique uuid-suffixed sku/location, cleaned up after) for a SKU at a location durably persists a stock_records row on the branch DB capturing sku, location, quantity, and combined inventory_code
retrieving a previously filed record (seeded under a unique uuid-suffixed key, cleaned up after) reads back the stored quantity and combined inventory_code exactly as filed

filing stock a second time for an already-filed (sku, location) pair (unique uuid-suffixed key, cleaned up after) updates the existing row in place so exactly one row remains, with no duplicate stored and no error surfaced
the routes/boundary module does not import the DB session; persistence lives only in the repository (layering contract)
the boundary returns JSON only and does no server-side template rendering (renders_via react, NFR-F1-5)
only the repository layer touches the ORM/session; the service and boundary contain no ORM imports (ORM-only persistence contract)
the connection string is sourced from the DATABASE_URL env var with no hardcoded connection string, pointing at the paired branch databricks_postgres (config-in-env, NFR-F1-7)
posting a body with an invalid/missing field to the boundary is rejected with an error payload that names the specific offending field rather than a generic bad-request (NFR-F1-6)
the service rejects an overcommitting/negative-quantity write at write time with no negative row persisted on the branch (NFR-F1-2 service-layer guard)
inserting two rows with the same (sku, location) directly against the branch DB raises a unique-constraint IntegrityError (verifies the migration realized PI1)
inserting a stock_records row with a NULL quantity (or NULL sku/location/inventory_code) directly against the branch DB is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint (verifies the migration realized PI2)
inserting a stock_records row with quantity = -1 directly against the branch DB is rejected by the CHECK (quantity >= 0) constraint (verifies the migration realized PI3)

the repository's read-existing-then-write upsert for a colliding (sku, location) runs in a single transaction against the branch so a concurrent repeat file resolves to one row and never stores two (verifies PI4)

the Alembic migration creating stock_records round-trips with a single-step downgrade -1 then upgrade head against an isolated branch and recreates the table + unique + check (verifies PI5 reversibility); marked @pytest.mark.migration
on an in-place upsert of an existing (sku, location) the original created_at timestamp is preserved unmodified (immutable audit timestamp, NFR-F1-1/R1)
the file-stock form renders its sku, location, quantity, and inventory_code fields plus its submit control with their data-testid seams (client component)
the stock-retrieval view renders the read-back quantity and combined inventory_code for a fetched record via its data-testid seams (client component)

reading the stock-by-location list through the boundary returns a JSON collection with one entry per seeded stock_records row (unique uuid-suffixed sku/location, cleaned up after) carrying that record's sku, location, and quantity, read through service and repository against the branch DB

read-path row shaping/ordering (the list DTO) lives in the service and the query is the repository's sole ORM touch; the boundary and React component contain no shaping or ORM logic (read-path layering contract)
the stock-by-location table component renders one row per record showing its SKU, location, and quantity via its data-testid seams (client component)
the quantity-column cells carry their right-align design-guide class / data-testid seam (the stable contract), asserted via the seam rather than any inline style or raw CSS (client component)

reading a location with no stock records (a unique uuid-suffixed location that owns no rows) through the boundary returns an empty JSON collection with a success status, not a 404 or error payload, read through service and repository against the branch DB
the table component maps an empty collection to the explicit "No stock at this location" empty state via its data-testid seam rather than a blank page (client component)

reading a SKU's detail through the boundary returns a JSON collection with one entry per location where that sku holds stock (seeded across multiple locations under a unique uuid-suffixed sku, cleaned up after), each entry carrying its location and quantity, read through service and repository against the branch DB

the SKU-detail group-by-location shaping (one entry per location for a sku) lives in the service and the sku-filtered query is the repository's sole ORM touch; the boundary and React component contain no shaping or ORM logic (detail read-path layering contract)
the SKU-detail component renders one row per location showing that location and its quantity via its data-testid seams (client component)

the SKU-detail read projection carries each entry's combined inventory_code through the boundary JSON (seed a record with a known inventory_code under a unique uuid-suffixed key, cleaned up after), read through service and repository against the branch DB
each SKU-detail location entry renders its combined inventory_code beside the location via its data-testid seam (client component)

for a seeded sku whose par_level is NULL (a unique uuid-suffixed sku, cleaned up after), the service maps the absent par_level to an explicit "not tracked" semantic in the boundary JSON (null is a valid state, never a null error), read through service and repository against the branch DB
the SKU-detail par-level region renders the explicit "not tracked" state (not a blank region or a null crash) when par_level is absent, via its data-testid seam (client component)

requesting the detail view for a sku that owns zero stock_records rows at any location (a unique uuid-suffixed sku that no test seeds) returns an empty JSON collection with a success status (200), never a 404 or null error, read through service and repository against the branch DB , absence grounded in observable zero rows, not a SKU registry
the SKU-detail component maps an empty collection to the explicit "No stock for this SKU" state via its data-testid seam, rather than a blank page or a null crash (client component)
